crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Tax Structuring and Planning
children.blurb: Tax structuring and planning is the practice of arranging a company's legal entities, transactions, and cash flows so that tax outcomes follow the commercial substance and the applicable rules.

children.name: Transfer Pricing
children.blurb: Transfer pricing is the set of rules and practices for setting and testing the prices charged in transactions between related entities that operate in different tax jurisdictions.

children.name: Research Credits from Engineering Records
children.blurb: Research credits from engineering records covers the use of engineering artifacts to support claims for research and development tax credits.

children.name: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
children.blurb: Sales, use, and value added tax are transaction taxes that apply to the transfer of goods and services.

children.name: Audit Defence and Controversy
children.blurb: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of responding to tax authority inquiries, audits, assessments, appeals, and mutual agreement procedures across jurisdictions.

sections.body: Tax and jurisdictional compliance for AI companies is the work of fitting a business that often spans many countries into tax rules that were not written with software, data and models in mind. In practice, AI teams use it to decide where to book revenue, where to hold intellectual property, how to price services between affiliates, and how to claim credits for engineering work. The field also covers indirect taxes on cloud services, data access and digital products, and it covers what happens when a tax authority questions a return. The work is not abstract: it shows up in intercompany agreements, invoices, payroll, royalty payments, and the records that support a research credit claim. AI itself is used here for document review, anomaly detection, and drafting, but the final positions still depend on human judgement and local law. The section is part of The AI Accountant, which looks at how AI changes accounting and finance work.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are well settled, such as basic sales tax registration and routine value added tax reporting for standard software subscriptions. Transfer pricing remains hard because AI value chains mix people, code, data, and servers in ways that do not map cleanly onto old rules. Research credits are often claimed from engineering records, but the link between a code commit, a design note, and a qualifying activity is not always clear, and auditors may challenge it. Structuring decisions are constrained by rules against avoidance, treaty networks, and changing international agreements, so a plan that works in one year may not survive the next. Audit defence is reactive and evidence heavy, and it depends on whether contemporaneous records exist. The site tracks 222 compliance and regulation pages, which shows how much of this work is about keeping current rather than finding a single permanent answer.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who needs to understand how an AI group is organised across borders would start with Tax Structuring and Planning, which sets out the main choices and their tradeoffs. Transfer Pricing goes deeper into how related entities charge each other for software, services, data, and intellectual property. Research Credits from Engineering Records explains how technical teams and tax teams can work from the same evidence, which matters when a claim is reviewed. Sales, Use and Value Added Tax covers the indirect taxes that apply to cloud, digital goods, and automated services in different places. Audit Defence and Controversy is the page for what happens after a filing is questioned, including how to assemble records and respond to information requests. Together these pages move from planning to pricing, from credits to indirect tax, and finally to dispute, which is the order in which many tax questions arise.
